questions.statement: It is round. You kick it and play soccer with it. What is it?
questions.context: En el recreo de un colegio de Barranquilla, los niños juegan fútbol en la cancha.

options.feedback: Correct. A ball is round and we kick it to play soccer.
Incorrect. A kite flies in the sky with a string; you do not kick it.
Incorrect. A doll looks like a little person; it is not round for soccer.
Incorrect. A puzzle has many pieces to put together; you do not kick it.

questions.explanation: La "ball" (pelota o balón) es redonda ("round") y se patea ("kick") para jugar fútbol. La cometa ("kite") vuela, la muñeca ("doll") parece una persona y el rompecabezas ("puzzle") tiene fichas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: It flies high in the sky on a windy day. You hold it with a long string. What is it?
questions.context: En agosto hace mucho viento en Villa de Leyva y las familias van a elevar cometas.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A toy car has wheels and moves on the floor; it does not fly.
Correct. A kite flies in the sky when it is windy, and you hold its string.
Incorrect. A yo-yo has a string, but it goes up and down in your hand; it does not fly.
Incorrect. A teddy bear is a soft toy animal that you hug; it cannot fly.

questions.explanation: La cometa se dice "kite" en inglés. Vuela alto ("flies high") cuando hay viento ("windy") y se sostiene con una cuerda larga ("string"). El yo-yo también tiene cuerda, pero no vuela.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: "I have a ___. It has two wheels and I ride it in the park."
questions.context: Daniel recibe un regalo de cumpleaños en Bucaramanga y lo usa en el parque.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A doll has no wheels and you do not ride it; you play with it like a baby.
Incorrect. A puzzle has pieces, not wheels, and you cannot ride it.
Incorrect. A kite has no wheels; it flies in the wind.
Correct. A bike has two wheels and you ride it.

questions.explanation: Las pistas son "two wheels" (dos ruedas) y "I ride it" (la monto). El juguete es la bicicleta, "bike". La estructura "I have a..." sirve para decir qué juguete tenemos: "I have a bike".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read the dialogue.
Teacher: "Is it your teddy bear, Valeria?"
Valeria: "Yes, ___"
questions.context: Al final de la clase en Pasto, la profesora encuentra un oso de peluche en una silla.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "I am" answers questions with "Are you...?", not "Is it...?"
Correct. A question with "Is it...?" gets the short answer "Yes, it is."
Incorrect. "It isn't" is a negative answer, so it does not go after "Yes".
Incorrect. "They are" is plural; the question asks about one teddy bear with "it".

questions.explanation: A la pregunta "Is it your...?" (¿es tuyo...?) se responde "Yes, it is." o "No, it isn't.". Como Valeria dice "Yes", la respuesta completa es "Yes, it is.". "I am" responde a "Are you...?".
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "Mateo's favorite toy is a spinning top. It is made of wood. He spins it on the floor with a string." What does Mateo do with his toy?
questions.context: Mateo vive en Medellín y su abuelo le regaló un trompo de madera.

options.text: He flies it in the sky.
options.feedback: Incorrect. We fly a kite in the sky, but the text says the top spins on the floor.
Incorrect. We ride a bike; a spinning top is too small to ride.
Incorrect. We put pieces together in a puzzle; a spinning top has no pieces.

options.text: He spins it on the floor.
options.feedback: Correct. The text says he spins the top on the floor with a string.

questions.explanation: El "spinning top" es el trompo, un juguete tradicional colombiano. El texto dice "He spins it on the floor": lo hace girar en el piso con una cuerda. Elevar es para la cometa y armar es para el rompecabezas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: Isabella escribe en su cuaderno de inglés sobre su juguete favorito en Cartagena.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Has" is used with he or she; with "I" the verb is "have".
Incorrect. "A" means one, so the noun must be singular: "a doll", not "a dolls".
Correct. With "I" we use "have", and "a" goes before one thing: "a doll".
Incorrect. The word order is wrong; the verb "have" goes after "I".

questions.explanation: La oración correcta sigue el orden sujeto + verbo + objeto: "I have a doll". Con "I" se usa "have" (no "has"), y después de "a" el sustantivo va en singular ("doll", no "dolls").
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "Laura has a puzzle, a yo-yo and two dolls. Her brother has a red car and a ball." Which sentence is TRUE?
questions.context: Laura y su hermano ordenan la caja de juguetes en su casa de Ibagué.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The red car belongs to her brother, not to Laura.
Incorrect. The yo-yo belongs to Laura; her brother has a car and a ball.
Correct. The text says Laura has two dolls.
Incorrect. The puzzle belongs to Laura, so this sentence is false.

questions.explanation: Hay que separar los juguetes de cada niño. Laura tiene rompecabezas, yo-yo y dos muñecas ("two dolls"). Su hermano tiene un carro rojo ("red car") y una pelota. Solo "Laura has two dolls" es verdadera.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Pablo finds a ball in the classroom. He wants to know if it belongs to his friend Sara. What does he ask her?
questions.context: Pablo encuentra un balón en el salón de clase en Santa Marta y quiere devolverlo a su dueño.

options.feedback: Correct. "Is it your ball?" asks if the ball belongs to Sara.
Incorrect. This asks what the object is, but Pablo already knows it is a ball.
Incorrect. Pablo has the ball in his hands, so he does not need to ask where it is.
Incorrect. This asks about what Sara likes, not about who owns the ball.

questions.explanation: Para preguntar de quién es algo usamos "Is it your...?" (¿es tuyo...?). Pablo ya sabe que es un balón y sabe dónde está; lo que quiere saber es si es de Sara: "Is it your ball?".
questions.subject: ingles
